results.notes: Randomized unit: individual writer; between-person design, so round=all and no first_round result. Condition coding: 1=Human-only, 2=Human with one GenAI idea, 3=Human with five GenAI ideas; this contrast uses treatment=[2], control=[1]. Keep writer records with participant._current_page_name=Finally; exclude the three human-condition writers reporting AI use in follow_up.1.player.used_ai_tool or its follow_up.2 fallback. This gives 95/100/98 writers. Retain all assigned AI-arm writers regardless of actual AI uptake. The two missing DAT scores do not exclude writers from these unconditional analyses. Keep evaluator records with participant._current_page_name=Finally, reshape their first-pass evaluator.{story_number}.player ratings, and inner join story_id to eligible writers. This drops 81 of 3600 ratings, retaining 3519 ratings from 600 evaluators; ratings were collected before AI-use disclosure. Every raw item rating, writer identifier, story identifier and condition matches the processed DTA. Outcome variable: eval_novel_index. Printed statistics are reproduced using rating-level OLS with both AI-arm indicators and Human-only reference; p-values use Stata's evaluator-clustered covariance correction G/(G-1)*(N-1)/(N-3) with G=600 and Student t with 599 df. The five-versus-one contrast uses the difference between the two coefficients in that same model. The reproduction n_units and study_n_analyzed refer to all three arms, not the pairwise contrast. For computed results, average all 9-14 ratings within each writer first, then weight writers equally. Thus computed participant means/differences can differ from printed rating-level values. The novelty index is the arithmetic mean of novel, original and rare, rebuilt in float64. Rebuilt indices match stored Stata indices within 3.2e-7 (float32 rounding). All printed checks must match at the printed precision before participant statistics are computed. SDs use denominator n-1. Difference is treatment mean minus control mean in the original units. Final difference_se is the HC2 sandwich SE from pairwise participant-level OLS on an intercept and treatment indicator; it equals sqrt(treatment_sd^2/n_treatment + control_sd^2/n_control). No clusters were randomized, so n_clusters is null.
